g.title: EleanorRank6Convo5 begins.
g.text: EleanorRank6Convo5 begins.

g.title: j1697518474
g.text: I was wondering, as I so often do...

g.title: j2754861435
g.text: Once this loop is finally closed, however that happens, what's next for Earth?

g.title: j611747352
g.text: I know 2000 is pretty far back in your past, but can you tell me ANYTHING about what's in store for our little planet?

g.title: j2457805742
g.text: It's not good, I'm afraid.

g.title: j1148708090
g.text: I don't think I should, honestly.

g.title: j911194856
g.text: From what little I can tell, Techrot becomes a global problem. People solve it with nukes - or try to.

g.title: j2974647671
g.text: If you're forewarned about what's coming you might try to change it, and that could mean I never exist.

g.title: j3281996348
g.text: That's how the first of the 'Radiation Wars' begins.

g.title: j1886771442
g.text: Call me selfish, but I like existing.

g.title: j3153599392
g.text: ... and eventually the planet gets so effed up that the Orokin want to bail out of it and go and live somewhere else, right?

g.title: j303677149
g.text: Oh, like everything you've done HASN'T changed the future?

g.title: j2623138926
g.text: ... which leads to the whole Zariman thing, which is where YOU come in.

g.title: j2033878403
g.text: You might have changed the little details, but the big ones have stayed pretty much the same.

g.title: j1309388909
g.text: Weird to think that it all starts right here in this city.

g.title: j1711704731
g.text: I think the Universe knows what she's doing.

g.title: j1874378931
g.text: Maybe that's partly why this year is so important.

g.title: j3561150224
g.text: Yeah. From Höllvania to the Zariman Ten-Zero. It's a throughline.

g.title: j3296245049
g.text: There's more going on than just blind particles mucking about.

g.title: j780975522
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j2073912276
g.text: hang about...

g.title: j3141260804
g.text: I don't share your view. The Universe is mindless.

g.title: j3726445784
g.text: I agree. If something as human as emotion can shape the Void...

g.title: j3684246175
g.text: Makes sense. If Albrecht's nuke had gone off would that mean no Techrot, so no knackered Earth, no need to escape, no first trip into the Void and no Indifference??

g.title: j2440686094
g.text: If yours was the Zariman Ten-Zero, what happened to Zarimans One through Nine?

g.title: j2927948029
g.text: Maybe from a very big or very small perspective, but not at the level where you and I exist.

g.title: j134935178
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j3792355819
g.text: ... I'm going to go see if Lettie has any coffee on the go.

g.title: j3388951279
g.text: Unmanned drones, from what I remember.

g.title: j1444433972
g.text: If we can make meaning and we're part of the Universe, then the Universe is by definition meaningful.

g.title: j2189692789
g.text: Exactly. The meaning we make isn't just comfortable delusion.

g.title: Chat ends.
g.text: Chat ends.

g.title: j1706227339
g.text: Or Cephalon-piloted terraforming pods. They experimented a LOT.

g.title: j1858560436
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j522398576
g.text: But there's always that voice whispering to you and insisting that none of this matters.

g.title: j1434359031
g.text: 'The Project', they called it.

g.title: j253307614
g.text: Our existence isn't any less true or valid than quarks or supernovas. We're important, like it or not.

g.title: j3995058019
g.text: Maybe the big cosmic throwdown isn't between Good and Evil, but meaning and meaninglessness?

g.title: j2543477165
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j176999024
g.text: Sounds better than 'Operation Get Our Irresponsible Arses To A New Planet That We Can Proceed To Shit All Over'.
